title: Climbing Stairs
description:
A staircase has `n` steps. From any step you may move up by one step or by two. Count the distinct move sequences that take you from the ground to exactly step `n`.

**Input format:** one line, the integer `n`.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: A single one-step move.

title: Coin Change
description:
You have an unlimited supply of coins in the denominations listed in `coins`. Find the smallest number of coins that total exactly `amount`, or report `-1` if that total cannot be formed.

**Input format:** line 1 is `coins` as a JSON array; line 2 is `amount`.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: Multiples of 4 never reach 7.
No coins are needed for a total of 0.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
A subsequence keeps some elements of `nums` in their original order, possibly skipping others. Return the length of the longest subsequence whose values are **strictly increasing**.

**Input format:** one line, `nums` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: One longest choice is 2, 3, 6, 9 (others have the same length).
Strictly increasing, so equal values can't both be used.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description:
Return the length of the longest sequence of characters that appears, in order but not necessarily contiguously, in **both** `text1` and `text2`. Return `0` if they share nothing.

**Input format:** line 1 is `text1` as a JSON string; line 2 is `text2`.

**Output format:** a single integer.
constraints:
- 1 <= text1.length, text2.length <= 1000
- Both contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: "pane" appears in order in both.
No common characters.
"oo" and "lo" share the best length, 2.

title: Word Break
description:
Decide whether `s` can be split into a sequence of one or more words from `wordDict`. Words may be reused any number of times.

**Input format:** line 1 is `s` as a JSON string; line 2 is `wordDict` as a JSON array of strings.

**Output format:** `true` or `false`.
constraints:
- 1 <= s.length <= 300
- 1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000
- 1 <= wordDict[i].length <= 20
- Lowercase English letters only; dictionary words are distinct

examples.explanation: "sun flower pot" works (so does "sunflower pot").
No word covers the "t" before "dog".
Words can repeat.

title: Combination Sum IV
description:
Given distinct positive integers `nums` and a `target`, count the **ordered** sequences of numbers from `nums` (each usable any number of times) that add up to `target`. Different orders count separately: `1 + 2` and `2 + 1` are two sequences. The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

**Input format:** line 1 is `nums` as a JSON array; line 2 is `target`.

**Output format:** a single integer.
constraints:
- 1 <= nums.length <= 200
- 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000, all distinct
- 1 <= target <= 1000
- The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

examples.explanation: No sequence reaches 3.

title: House Robber
description:
Houses stand in a row, and `nums[i]` is the money in house `i`. You may take money from any houses, except that you can never take from **two adjacent houses**. Return the most money you can collect.

**Input format:** one line, `nums` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: Take 10 and 6: 16.
Take the first and last houses: 10.

title: House Robber II
description:
The same rule as **House Robber**: no two adjacent houses. But now the houses stand in a **circle**, so the first and last houses are also neighbours. Return the most money you can collect.

**Input format:** one line, `nums` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** a single integer.

examples.explanation: The first and last houses now touch, so at most one of the 5s: 6.
A single house has no neighbours.

title: Decode Ways
description:
Letters are encoded as numbers: `A` → `1`, `B` → `2`, …, `Z` → `26`. Given a string of digits `s`, count the ways to split it into pieces that are each a valid code (`1` to `26`, with no leading zero) and so decode it back into letters.

The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

**Input format:** one line, `s` as a JSON string.

**Output format:** a single integer.
constraints:
- 1 <= s.length <= 100
- `s` contains only digits
- The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

examples.explanation: Only 20 6 works: "06" has a leading zero and "2 06" isn't allowed.
"30" is too big and "0" alone isn't a code.

title: Unique Paths
description:
A robot starts in the top-left corner of an `m × n` grid and must reach the bottom-right corner, moving only **right** or **down**. Count the different paths it can take. The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

**Input format:** line 1 is `m` (rows); line 2 is `n` (columns).

**Output format:** a single integer.
constraints:
- 1 <= m, n <= 100
- The answer is at most 2 × 10^9

examples.explanation: Each path makes 2 right moves and 2 down moves in some order: 6 orders.
A single row has only one path.

title: Jump Game
description:
You start at index `0`. From index `i` you may jump forward by any distance from `1` to `nums[i]`. Decide whether you can reach the **last index**.

**Input format:** one line, `nums` as a JSON array.

**Output format:** `true` or `false`.

examples.explanation: Jump 2 to index 2, then 2 more to the end.
Every route gets stuck on the 0 at index 2.
You're already on the last index.
